newsitem.title: UK: GA Life says new premium income up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: GA Life says new premium income up 15 pct.

text.p: British insurance group General Accident Life said on Wednesday that total new premium income rose 15 percent in 1996 to 1.08 billion stg and showed strong growth in all its main business areas.
New annual premiums doubled to 84.8 million stg while new single premiums rose 11.5 percent to 996.1 million stg.
New annualised premium income (new annual premiums plus a tenth of new single premiums) rose 40 percent to 184.4 million stg.
"This was a good year for General Accident Life by any measure but, on top of considerable growth in 1995, I believe it was an exceptional year," said assistant general manager Peter Hales.
"New business growth is well in line with our long term growth strategy and has been achieved across all business areas. Of particular note is our growth in pensions business."
Pensions new annualised premium income was 86.9 million stg in 1996 compared with 29.9 million stg the previous year.
Total premium income for pensions was 453.4 million stg, up from 220.3 million stg in 1995.
